# ggTrader Strategy Research Snapshot

**Regenerated by:** `.claude/skills/research-snapshot`
**Last full regeneration:** 2026-09-23
**Scope:** Strategy-research verdicts only (not ops/deployment/infra history —
see `docs/next_steps.md` and `docs/research/artifacts-2026-09-09-perf-review/`
for the live paper-trading operational picture).

This file is fully regenerated from source of truth each time the
`research-snapshot` skill runs — it is not meant to be hand-edited
incrementally. The 2026-09-23 regeneration moves the baseline a fourth
time: the 0.99 core figure cited from 2026-08-22 was itself inflated by a
point-in-time (PIT) index-membership leak in every signal-strategy sweep
(fixed `c9d1abe`). Under PIT membership **the core no longer beats SPY.**

---

## 1. Current validated baseline — the bar to beat

**The bar is now SPY buy-and-hold.** No strategy in this lab currently beats
it on a pinned window with point-in-time membership.

**5-voter `EnsembleSignal` core** (`bb_reversion` + `rsi_reversion` +
`ema_cross` + `macd_divergence` + `volume_bb_reversion`), flat 3.3% sizing per
entry, SP500 universe, 1.0x leverage. Pinned 17-fold walk-forward
(2021-01-31 → 2026-04-30), corrected tape, daily PIT S&P 500 membership mask
on entries:

| | OOS Sharpe | CAGR | MaxDD | Gates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SP500 core, PIT** | **0.59** | **3.1%** | **-5.3%** | 17/17 |
| SP500 core, pre-PIT (2026-08-22) — *leak-inflated, do not cite* | 0.99 | 8.0% | -7.65% | 12/17 |
| **SPY, same window** | **0.78** | **13.0%** | **-22.1%** | — |

(`docs/research/2026-09-23-pit-rebaseline-core-nogo.md`, raw
`docs/research/_pit_rebaseline_20260923.json`.) Before `c9d1abe`, the WFO
generated entries for every stock loaded over 2021–2026 whether or not it
was an index member that day; 14.1% of core entries fell on non-member days
(`docs/research/2026-09-23-ic-kelly-rebaseline-invalid.md`). Folds 6–8 have
NaN Sharpe because the selected `min_agree=4` combos barely trade — the
stitched curve counts those months as cash, which is what the strategy
would actually have done.

**What the core still is:** a low-drawdown, low-return sleeve (-5.3% MaxDD
vs SPY's -22.1%, 17/17 gate pass). It is not an index-beater. The live
paper account runs this core (reverted from the 3-sleeve blend, deployed
2026-09-22) plus an idle-cash SPY sweep; how much to allocate to the
stock-picking sleeve vs. SPY is an open owner decision.

**How to judge a new lever against this bar:**
- A standalone strategy must beat SPY's **0.78 Sharpe** on the pinned window
  — beating the core's 0.59 is not enough.
- A diversifier/sleeve can instead be judged on whether it improves a
  **SPY + sleeve** portfolio's Sharpe or drawdown over SPY alone.
- Any signal-strategy number must come from a run with a `universe_fn`
  wired (PIT mask on); `run_wfo` now warns if it isn't.

The 3-sleeve blend's 0.69 (2026-08-22) predates the PIT fix, is no longer
live, and should not be cited as a current comparison.

## 3. What worked, structurally

Methodology/infrastructure wins, independent of any one strategy's verdict —
more durable than the roster above:

- **The lab/WFO rewrite itself.** Moving from the pre-rewrite `research/`
  package to `src/ggTrader/lab/` (vectorbt-centric, DB-backed walk-forward)
  is what made every later verdict in §2 trustworthy — before that, momentum/
  tournament verdicts weren't run through the same rigorous gate framework.
- **NDH/DSR/gate discipline.** Requiring a strategy to clear a
  density-of-history gate and a deflated-Sharpe-ratio check before "winning"
  a fold catches noise-driven false positives (the leveraged-rotation arc's
  regime-halt mechanism correctly refused to trust an unstable winner).
- **Flat, simple sizing beats conviction-weighting.** 3.3% flat per entry is
  the live config; conviction-weighted sizing (`conviction_bb`) was shipped
  and tested but generated no extra profit — simplicity won.
- **Root-caused and fixed a whole-tape, one-calendar-day mislabeling bug
  (2026-08-20).** A tz-aware UTC index written into a naive-timestamp column
  let Postgres rebase every one of ~5.68M equity bars across 1,412 symbols
  one day early (`CachedYFinanceLoader._cache_to_db`), and a second SPY-only
  writer left 826 duplicate rows deflating the benchmark's Sharpe ~29%. Both
  fixed and migrated in place; every WFO run since is on a clean,
  reproducible tape. See `docs/next_steps.md` "RESOLVED (2026-08-20/22)" for
  the full mechanism and blast-radius analysis.
- **Pin `--eval-start`/`--eval-end` on any run whose number will be cited,
  and use SPY's own re-measured Sharpe as a drift control.** The unrecoverable
  1.12/1.14 baseline traced entirely to an unpinned `--eval-end` defaulting
  to "now" — proven because SPY's own Sharpe (which cannot itself change)
  read differently across citations of the "same" window
  (`docs/research/2026-08-19-anchor-fix-reproduction.md`).
- **Leverage-realism as a prerequisite for diversification claims — and even
  leverage-realistic diversification can still lose.** Multi-universe equity
  blending only became a real contender once capped at a realistic 1.0x
  leverage via inverse-vol/target-vol weighting; even so, the corrected-tape
  re-baseline shows that blend now trailing the standalone core (§1) — a
  leverage-realistic construction is necessary but not sufficient.
- **Universe membership function matters** — `universe_members_asof(...,
  pd.Timestamp.now())` is the survivorship-biased choice, not the fix;
  `equity_universe_between` (span-union) is the safer lab default
  (`docs/research/2026-08-18-wfo-anchor-leakage-fix.md`).
- **Always benchmark timing/rotation ideas against naive buy-and-hold of the
  same instrument, not just SPY.** This flipped the leveraged-trend arc's
  read from "looks promising" (low drawdown!) to NO-GO (loses to just
  holding the ETF), and did the same for the FX-hedge and Treasury-curve
  dynamic-vs-static comparisons.
- **`target_kind="weights"` vs `"signals"` changes which overlays apply.**
  The realized-vol-targeting overlay is wired only into `simulate_signals`,
  not `simulate_weights` — choosing the wrong `target_kind` silently drops
  an intended risk control.
- **Free, structured bulk-data sources exist in more places than expected —
  check before assuming "paid data."** FINRA short-interest/short-volume,
  SEC EDGAR Form 4, House Clerk PTR disclosures, and Google Trends all had
  genuine multi-year depth once actually queried.
- **...but point-in-time fundamentals/estimates/options and permno-keyed
  academic datasets are reliably paid-only, no matter how many free sources
  are checked** — four independent candidates hit this same wall (#2, #7,
  #4, #14). A fast, cheap pre-check now: does the free source expose a
  genuine point-in-time *history*, or only a current snapshot?
- **Daily PIT membership mask on signal-strategy entries (2026-09-23,
  `c9d1abe`).** `pit_entry_mask()` in `lab/sweep.py` builds a daily boolean
  mask from `universe_fn` and ANDs it into entries only (exits and sizing
  untouched), threaded through the anchor, train, test and live sweeps in
  `run_wfo`. It cut the core from 0.99 to 0.59 Sharpe — the single largest
  bias correction in the project's history. Coverage checked at 483–501 of
  ~503 members (gap = renames and recent spin-offs under the 400-bar
  minimum). Load data with `equity_universe_between` (span union) **and**
  pass `universe_fn=eligible_at(...)` so the per-day mask applies.
- **Pre-registered verdict criteria.** The IC/Kelly re-run fixed its
  pass bar (Sharpe > 1.05 and above control, MaxDD ≥ -10%, top winner ≥
  8/17 folds) before running — and the first run's 38% Kelly CAGR, which
  would otherwise have looked like a breakthrough, was traced to a single
  garbage bar (SIVB $0.0013 → $0.11 after its index exit) instead of being
  reported.
- **`simulate_weights` needs an all-empty-combo guard** — a fold where every
  grid combo picks zero symbols degenerates `vbt.Portfolio.from_orders` to
  zero groups and crashes rather than returning a flat-cash curve; fixed
  with a short-circuit in `simulate.py`.

## 4. What failed, grouped by root cause

- **Survivorship leakage inflated every signal-strategy result until
  2026-09-23.** Signal sweeps traded any stock in the loaded span on any
  day, including days before it joined or after it left the S&P 500 —
  which is exactly where mean-reversion finds its biggest bounces (and
  garbage post-delisting bars). Removing it took the core from "beats SPY"
  (0.99) to "loses to SPY" (0.59). Lesson: a mean-reversion edge on single
  stocks is extremely sensitive to universe definition; any future equity
  result must be checked for membership leakage *before* it is believed.
- **A one-day tape mislabeling gave every event-date study an undetected
  lookahead advantage, and they still failed.** Before the 2026-08-20 fix,
  every equity bar was stamped one calendar day early, so any strategy
  joining on a real-world calendar date (PEAD, Form 4 insider buying,
  Congressional PTR mirroring, short-interest, FOMC dates) was effectively
  trading on tomorrow's price today. **Because PEAD, insider cluster-buying,
  and Congressional trades still failed to beat SPY or improve the blend
  *with* that lookahead edge, they will certainly perform worse without it —
  their NO-GOs are not just intact, they are stronger than originally
  reported.** `fomc_drift` is the single exception: its calendar-date
  workaround for a separate timestamp quirk meant the shifted tape made it
  test literally the wrong day (the announcement day, not the day before),
  so its NO-GO is the one genuinely voided by the bug — see §6 Tier 2.
  (`docs/research/2026-09-10-comprehensive-strategy-audit-and-retry-recommendations.md`
  §4)
- **Signal-strength-as-timing doesn't survive contact with real cost/decay.**
  ML entry gate (P(up) anti-predictive), both leveraged-ETF arcs (breadth
  and trend-filter timing both lost to simpler/no-timing alternatives). A
  signal that looks predictive in isolation doesn't automatically translate
  into a profitable entry/exit *timing* rule once real transaction costs,
  leveraged-ETF decay, or regime-halt dynamics are in play.
- **Added complexity underperforms the simpler default.** MTF reversion
  (6th voter), the 6-indicator ensemble, IC-weighted voting, Kelly sizing,
  conviction-weighted sizing — every attempt to make the ensemble "smarter"
  than flat-vote/flat-size has lost to the simpler baseline, and the
  PIT re-run of 2026-09-23 confirmed it for `ensemble_ic` (0.41) and
  `ensemble_kelly` (0.50), both below the 0.59 core.
- **Equity diversification is correlation-capped, and leverage-realism alone
  doesn't fix it.** Naive multi-universe blending lost to the SP500 core
  alone; the leverage-realistic version (inverse-vol/target-vol weighted)
  briefly looked like a fix but the corrected-tape re-baseline shows it
  *still* trails the core (§1) — the diversification value being sought
  from same-asset-class equity sleeves appears structurally capped.
- **Momentum/tournament-style ranking is well-arbitraged in large-cap
  equities** — both the pre-rewrite and (still unverified on the current
  stack, see §6) implementations show negative/flat risk-adjusted
  performance historically.
- **Regime/volatility gates applied as a blunt entry filter don't help** —
  VIX-level regime throttling rejected; distinct from a *sizing* overlay
  (vol-target blend weighting, which is structurally sound even though the
  blend as a whole now underperforms) — the failure mode is specifically
  "binary gate on entries."
- **Nine consecutive same-asset-class diversification-sleeve candidates
  failed via one of three distinct signatures**, none of which is
  overfitting in the classic sense:
  - *Eval-window-drift* (PEAD, insider cluster-buying, Congressional
    trades): a long, earlier-starting backtest window shows a real-looking
    result concentrated in a period the deployed blend's actual validated
    window doesn't cover.
  - *High correlation to the existing core* (MAX-effect: 0.692 correlation,
    the highest measured).
  - *No signal at the fidelity available* (short-volume-ratio,
    short-interest, commodity trend, FX hedge, Treasury curve): mechanically
    correct constructions with near-zero or negative excess Sharpe — not
    overfitting, just genuinely no edge (or, for the FX/Treasury dynamic
    overlays, real edge that a static baseline captures for free).
  - **Standing takeaway: another same-asset-class, same-market equity
    cross-sectional signal is increasingly unlikely to clear this bar.**
    Diversification value probably needs a different asset class, geography,
    or time horizon — see §6 Tier 1.
- **Deep historical point-in-time data is reliably paid-only.** Four
  independent candidates (analyst-revision momentum, Anomaly-Driven Demand,
  options IV skew, crypto funding-rate carry) all hit this same wall on
  inspection, despite looking different on the surface. Fast, cheap
  first-check for any new candidate: does the free source expose a genuine
  point-in-time *history*, or only a current snapshot/short rolling window?

## 5. Known documentation gaps

- ⚠️ **Pre-PIT signal-strategy verdicts are unre-measured.** Every
  signals-kind NO-GO before 2026-09-23 (see the caveat under §2) lacked PIT
  membership. They were mostly rejected for trailing a core that was
  itself inflated, so under PIT both sides move. No re-run has been done.
  Wide misses vs SPY (`overnight_gap` -0.01, `mtf_reversion` 0.49) are safe
  to leave closed; anything that failed *only* against the phantom core is
  unresolved against SPY — though as variants of a core that now loses to
  SPY, their prior is low (see §6).
- ⚠️ **`docs/roadmap.md` is stale.** Its top-of-file note still cites core

## 6. Internally-derived candidate ideas

These are reasoned from *what's failed and why* (§4), cross-checked against
the independent priority queue in
`docs/research/2026-09-10-comprehensive-strategy-audit-and-retry-recommendations.md`
§5, which converges on largely the same picks from a fresh full-repo audit.
For genuinely new ideas sourced from outside literature/practice, see
`docs/research/WEB_RESEARCH_CANDIDATES.md` (a separate, accumulating
backlog — all 14 of its original candidates are resolved; it needs a fresh
discovery pass before it has new material to triage). Both feed the same
next step: pick a candidate, fill it into
`docs/research/prompts/local-implementation-prompt-TEMPLATE.md`, queue it in
`docs/next_steps.md`.

The don't-re-propose list embedded in both prompt files (§2/§4 above,
condensed) is kept in sync with this section — do not edit one without the
other.

**What changed this run:** the PIT re-baseline turned the question from
"what beats a 0.99 core" into "what beats or usefully complements SPY at
0.78". That demotes every idea that is a variant of the reversion core,
closes constrained `ensemble_ic` (its unconstrained parent scored 0.41 —
there is nothing for a weight floor to stabilize toward), and promotes
anything with a different return source.

### Tier 1 — highest prior (zero new data cost)

1. **Cross-asset trend/risk-parity sleeve (`TLT`/`GLD`/`DBC`, unleveraged).**
   The strongest case in the list: a different macro risk factor
   (duration, gold, commodity trend), free daily OHLCV already kept fresh
   by the live tape keepalive, and no index-membership exposure at all.
   `leveraged_trend_*` failed on leveraged-ETF decay, not the trend logic.
   Judge it as a complement: does SPY + sleeve beat SPY alone on Sharpe
   (0.78) and MaxDD (-22.1%) on the pinned window? Benchmark each leg
   against its own buy-and-hold too.
2. **Re-test `xs_momentum`/`dual_momentum` on the current lab stack.** Weight
   strategies were already PIT-correct, so this is a clean first modern
   measurement of a NO-GO that traces to deleted code. `dual_momentum`'s
   absolute-momentum leg (go to cash/bonds in downtrends) is also the one
   documented way to cut SPY's -22% drawdown without stock-picking.
   Success bar: Sharpe > 0.78 vs SPY on the pinned window, gates ≥ 12/17.

### Tier 2 — lower effort or lower prior

3. **`fomc_drift` retest on the true pre-announcement bar.** The only
   event-study NO-GO voided (not merely lookahead-advantaged) by the tape
   bug; ETF universe, so unaffected by PIT; compute is trivial (<5 min).
4. **Commodity carry / roll yield (candidate A2).** Distinct from the
   rejected `commodity_trend` (price momentum); reuses A3's 14-ETF universe.
   ETF roll-yield proxies are only approximations of futures carry — flag
   that in the design.
5. **PIT re-screen of near-miss signal NO-GOs against SPY.** Cheap to run
   (existing driver, `--strategies`), but low prior: every candidate is a
   variant of a reversion core that now loses to SPY by 0.19 Sharpe. Only
   worth doing for completeness of the record, or if Tier 1 finds a
   reason to keep investing in single-stock reversion.
6. **`retail_attention` backfill retry** with slower Google Trends pacing —
   code and 19 unit tests are complete; only data collection blocks a
   verdict.

**Dropped this run:** constrained `ensemble_ic` (closed by the PIT re-run).
International developed-market rotation and yield-curve duration timing
stay dropped from the prior run — Tier 1 #1 covers the same
different-asset-class thesis more directly.
